title: Captain Polyplast Ltd - 536974 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR142 crore (up ~80% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 9.96% on March raw-material spike.
summary.overview: Management, represented by Whole-time Director Ritesh Khichadia, reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR142 crore versus INR79.1 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA up 66% to INR14.16 crore and margin down 86 bps YoY to 9.96%. Net profit rose 91% to INR9.76 crore (EPS INR1.64). Full-year FY26 total income was INR419 crore (up 44%), EBITDA INR6.32 crore at an 11.03% margin, per the call. Management attributed margin compression to raw-material price increases in March 2026 and highlighted the Ahmedabad plant going operational and a credit rating upgrade during FY26.

segments.name: Micro-irrigation (core)
segments.commentary: Subsidy-linked business remains the bulk of revenue; cash/non-subsidy contribution was about 15% in FY26. Export is about 5% of micro-irrigation revenue, targeted to reach double digits in five years. Management targets 20-25% average growth over the next three years.

segments.name: Solar pumps (EPC)
segments.commentary: Order book built mainly on Maharashtra PM-KUSUM work (~1,500 pumps in FY26). A new 500-pump order worth ~INR11 crore was received in Q4; about 1,000 pumps were executed in the prior quarter and at least 1,000 are targeted this quarter.

segments.name: Solar rooftop (EPC)
segments.commentary: Expanded to multiple states under PM Surya Ghar Yojana, targeting tier-2/3/4 markets; fully cash business per management. Management sees it as a counter to micro-irrigation seasonality (about six selling months).

guidance_outlook: Micro-irrigation business EBITDA margin expected to improve by 1-1.5 percentage points once the Ahmedabad plant is fully operational in FY27.
Micro-irrigation revenue targeted to grow at 20-25% average over the next three years.
Target to bring solar EPC contribution to about 50:50 with micro-irrigation within two years, from roughly 80:20 currently.
Working capital intensity expected to stabilise in FY27 on receivable recoveries.
Current capacity can deliver about INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue for the next couple of years without additional capex.
Management did not provide a consolidated EBITDA margin for FY27.
capex_capacity: Ahmedabad plant (about 70,000 sq ft) is now operational; it will in-source high-margin micro-irrigation components.
Existing capacity at Rajkot and Kurnool plus Ahmedabad supports ~INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue without additional capex.
Capex intensity expected to stay modest; working capital is the main incremental capital need.
Multiple micro-irrigation components run on the same extrusion lines, so utilisation percentage was not disclosed.
Management is targeting empanelment for PM-KUSUM in additional states in FY27.
demand_pricing: Government policy support for micro-irrigation and solar pumps seen as continuing; PM-KUSUM budget maintained for the current year.
Solar pump margins described as similar to micro-irrigation margins, so management sees no dilution from mix.
Q4 margin decline attributed to a sharp March 2026 rise in raw-material prices from geopolitical events.
Micro-irrigation penetration is about 17-18% of the ~70 million hectare potential; under-penetration above 80%.
Solar pump tenders are L1-based with matching by other bidders and quantum allocated by historical execution; no bidding pipeline disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the solar mix diluting margins and is the working capital cycle stretching cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 margin fell mainly on raw-material costs, with pump margins similar to micro-irrigation. Working capital rose with high growth and is expected to stabilise on receivable recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR50 crore SBI credit line is drawn to backstop subsidy delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the figure. Total debt was about INR89 crore at end-March, and unutilised bank limits were about 30-35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between subsidy and cash sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash contribution in micro-irrigation was about 15% in FY26; rooftop solar is entirely cash business and additional to that.

qa_highlights.question: What unexecuted solar order book exists and what is the execution run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The unexecuted order is about 500 pumps worth ~INR11 crore. Management targets at least 1,000 pumps executed in the current quarter, after about 1,000 in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much can the Ahmedabad plant lift micro-irrigation margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects micro-irrigation EBITDA margin to rise by 1-1.5 percentage points once the plant is fully running this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company supply irrigation accessories to third parties?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for now; the focus is on captive use first, with third-party sales to be evaluated after the captive business scales.

risks_watch: Raw-material price volatility, which drove the Q4 margin decline; no pass-through mechanism was discussed.
Working capital intensity and receivables from state subsidy disbursement cycles; watch whether intensity eases in FY27.
Dependence of the solar pump order book on Maharashtra tenders; the unexecuted book is small (~INR11 crore).
Pricing competition from regional and unorganised players, and subsidy timing variability.
Execution of the Ahmedabad ramp-up and whether the 1-1.5 pp margin uplift materialises.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, policy support and capacity, but cautious and sometimes vague on specifics: it declined to disclose the credit-line drawdown, the utilisation rate and an FY27 margin guide, and answered a plastic-pipe question by deflecting to micro-irrigation.
key_quotes: So, this transition which we have dedicatedly focused on improving the mix, this is a gradual process by design, but we believe that it will improve the overall quality and predictability of our micro-irrigation revenues as we go ahead.
No, as I said in my remarks as well, the primary reason for decline in EBITDA margin was the increase in raw material costs, especially during the month of March.
So, definitely working capital is something which is fungible and which can be changed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR79.1 crore in Q4 FY25 (~80% YoY)

adds.what: Ahmedabad plant (~70,000 sq ft) in-sourcing high-margin micro-irrigation components, now operational

growth.why: Management targets 20-25% average micro-irrigation revenue growth over three years and says existing Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad capacity supports ~INR400 crore revenue without capex, with Ahmedabad adding 1-1.5 pt margin uplift in FY27; backing is partial (capacity and PM-KUSUM order flow, but no utilisation figure and no pipeline disclosed).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided micro-irrigation EBITDA margin up 1-1.5 pp once the Ahmedabad plant (~70,000 sq ft, now operational) is fully running in FY27, though Q4 FY26 margin fell to 9.96% (down 86 bps YoY) on March raw-material spike and no consolidated FY27 margin was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Existing Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad capacity supports ~INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue for the next couple of years without additional capex, versus FY26 total income of INR419 crore, so no new plant is needed in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 20-25% average micro-irrigation revenue growth over three years, Q4 FY26 revenue rose ~80% YoY to INR142 crore, and solar pump execution is targeted at at least 1,000 pumps this quarter after ~1,000 last quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex intensity is expected to stay modest, capacity covers ~INR400 crore revenue without capex, and utilisation was not disclosed, so no new capex announcement is signalled; working capital is the main capital need.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Growth is strong (Q4 FY26 revenue +80% YoY, FY26 total income +44%) and PM-KUSUM budget is maintained, but management gave no formal FY27 consolidated guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw-material volatility drove the Q4 margin fall with no pass-through mechanism discussed, working capital intensity is high, and the solar order book is small (~INR11 crore unexecuted), so margin or cash targets could slip.

rows.label: PM-KUSUM empanelment in additional states
rows.why: Management is targeting empanelment in more states in FY27, but Maharashtra currently drives the solar pump order book (~1,500 pumps in FY26) and no pipeline was disclosed.

rows.label: Solar rooftop expansion under PM Surya Ghar Yojana
rows.why: Rooftop has expanded to multiple states, targets tier-2/3/4 markets, and is a fully cash business that offsets micro-irrigation's ~six selling months, with management aiming for solar EPC to reach about 50:50 with micro-irrigation within two years from roughly 80:20 now.

rows.label: Working capital intensity stabilises
rows.why: Management expects working capital to stabilise in FY27 on receivable recoveries, but no figures were given and total debt was about INR89 crore at end-March with 30-35% unutilised bank limits.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20-25% growth, policy support and existing capacity covering ~INR400 crore revenue, but was cautious on the credit-line drawdown, utilisation and FY27 margin, and deflected a plastic-pipe question; analysts pressed on solar margin dilution and working capital.
